children: U.K. inflation should remain above the Bank of England's 2% target for a while, with a November rate rise all but guaranteed, says Thomas Pugh at RSM UK following the latest U.K. inflation data. Inflation rose to 3.5% in September, driven by fuel prices, with higher energy, food and memory chip costs expected to push inflation higher, he says. "We see inflation peaking at 4.5% in early 2027 and doubt it will be back at 2% until 2028." Still, knock-on effects from higher energy prices remain limited. "The [Monetary Policy Committee] will take some comfort that the miss was almost entirely driven by fuel prices and that there is little sign of second round effects so far." Pugh expects another rate rise in 2027. (don.forbes@wsj.com)
